decisions.executionNote: Approach the charger with the left arm, gradually pitching down while preserving the initial elbow branch; right arm stays clear.
Continue left pregrasp approach with small, continuous pitch increments; charger remains on table.
Finish pitching the left gripper toward the charger and advance above it, keeping the jaws open.
Lower toward the charger, correcting its leftward wrist-image offset and small yaw misalignment.
Fine approach to the charger body with open jaws; align its long edges in the wrist image before closing.
Correct the charger’s wrist-image offset at constant height before closing; avoid advancing into its front edge.
Center the charger between the left jaws and close fully; retention will be checked during a small lift.
Make a small wrist-image centering correction, then close the left gripper on the charger body.
Hold the left gripper fully closed and lift 2 cm to verify that the charger follows the hand.
Charger follows the left gripper in RGB. Lift clear of the table and start moving toward the central handoff area, keeping the grasp closed.
Rotate the held charger toward a central handoff and begin positioning the open right gripper from its own workspace; use small continuous rotations.
Continue the elevated handoff approach, keeping the charger secure and the two wrists on their respective sides.
Carry the charger toward the central handoff while the open right gripper turns inward. Maintain separated wrist paths.
Complete most of the left handoff orientation and bring the open right hand nearer, still with clearance between grippers.
Stabilize the left hand at the central handoff pose and align the open right gripper with the exposed charger body.
Advance the open right gripper toward the exposed end of the charger while the left hand holds still; finish opposing wrist alignment.
Bring the open right jaws around the exposed charger body, with a small lateral centering correction. Left maintains its grasp.
Seat the right jaws around the charger body and close, keeping the left grasp until the transfer can be checked visually.
Let the right grip settle fully closed, then release the left jaws without moving either wrist.
Separate the wrists after handoff, keeping the right grip closed and checking that the charger follows it.
Charger is retained by the right hand. Lift and gradually rotate it toward upright above the right-side power strip.
The prior motion was rejected without movement. Retry the upright rotation with half-sized increments to preserve joint continuity.
Continue the slow upright rotation and elevated approach, retaining the charger in the right jaws.
Continue turning the charger upright while raising it for clearance over the right-side power strip.
Maintain the secure right grasp and progressively align its insertion axis vertically above the strip.
Continue the upright rotation above the strip with clearance, keeping the right grip closed and the left arm stationary.
Bring the charger close to vertical over the middle socket while retaining height for final visual alignment.
Finish the vertical insertion orientation and align the charger’s pin-pair direction with the power strip before descending.
Lower the upright charger toward the middle socket and correct its small lateral offset, retaining a gap above the strip.
Correct the socket’s fore-aft offset in the wrist view while lowering slowly; keep the charger upright and closed in the jaws.
Make small lateral and yaw corrections over the middle socket, then continue a slow vertical approach.
Press the aligned charger straight down in small increments toward insertion depth, without lateral motion.
Pause at the reached depth, then release the right jaws without disturbing the charger so its seating can be checked.
Lift the open right gripper clear to inspect the charger’s retention in the socket, and begin returning the left arm along a continuous elbow-up path.
The charger remains on the strip after release. Move both open hands clear and gradually unwind toward their home configurations.
Continue returning the empty arms with open jaws, lifting away from the seated charger and preserving elbow-up continuity.
The charger appears to have tipped during withdrawal. Stop rotation and lift the right gripper vertically clear before reassessing and recovering it.
The charger is tipped beside the socket. Reorient the open right hand above clear space for a new grasp from its exposed end; continue parking the left arm.
Unwind the right wrist in clear space for the recovery approach; bring the left hand closer to its origin without crossing workspaces.
Park the left arm and continue the right wrist's gradual recovery orientation, staying clear of the tipped charger.
Continue turning the open right gripper toward the exposed charger end, with a gradual approach above the table. Left remains at home.
Approach the recovery grasp gradually while turning the right jaws toward the charger; keep them open and clear of the strip.
Continue the right-hand recovery alignment in small increments, approaching from the exposed end rather than over the sockets.
Continue orienting the right gripper along the fallen charger’s body, maintaining a gradual descent with open jaws.
Finish most of the end-on recovery orientation, keeping clearance above the fallen charger before final centering.
Align the recovery gripper with the fallen charger’s long axis and lower toward its exposed end, without closing yet.
Center the fallen charger in the open right jaws using the wrist view, with a shallow descent toward its body.
Continue centering the exposed charger body between the open right jaws, using small lateral and forward corrections.
Close the right jaws on the centered fallen charger body and let the grasp settle before lifting.
Lift the closed right gripper slightly to verify recovery of the charger, without rotating against the strip.
The charger did not follow the lift. Reopen and lower the right jaws further around its body for a deeper grasp.
Lower the right jaws to the charger’s sidewall height, correct centering, and close for another retention test.
Let the deeper grasp settle closed, then lift gently to verify that the charger is retained.
The charger now follows the right hand. Lift it clear of the strip with the grip closed before turning the pins downward.
Raise the retained charger and begin turning its currently horizontal pin axis downward; account for the inclined end-on grasp rather than assuming EE vertical means charger vertical.
Continue raising and pitching the securely held charger toward pins-down while moving toward the socket with clearance.
Continue the pins-down rotation in clear space, carrying the charger toward the socket while retaining the end-on grasp.
Continue rotating the recovered charger toward upright and compensate its pin-tip arc with a forward motion above the socket.
Rotate beyond EE-vertical so the charger itself approaches upright, compensating the end-on grasp offset while remaining above the strip.
Complete the approximately ninety-degree rotation of the charger from its recovered flat pose, leaving clearance for pin-to-socket alignment.
Approach the middle socket with the charger now pins-down, using the visible pin tips and slot row for gradual alignment rather than committing to insertion.
Bring the visible pin pair toward the middle socket’s parallel slots with small lateral and downward corrections, maintaining the closed grasp.
Make a millimetric lateral correction at the pin tips, then lower vertically in small steps while retaining the charger for seating inspection.
Relieve vertical contact and correct the remaining fore-aft pin-to-slot offset at nearly constant height before another straight insertion attempt.
The pin pair is visually aligned with the parallel slots. Lower straight down by small increments, keeping the grasp closed for seating verification.
Apply a final shallow vertical seating motion and pause with the charger supported; do not release or rotate until its seated pose can be checked.
Release at the reached seating depth without moving the wrist, then check whether the charger remains upright before withdrawing along the approach axis.
Withdraw the fully open right jaws along the reverse approach direction, without rotation, to avoid contacting the charger during the seating check.
The charger did not remain seated after withdrawal. Clear the strip and return toward the recovery grasp, preserving the same elbow-up branch.
Return toward a side grasp of the unseated charger. Its visible pins indicate the orientation must be corrected before another insertion attempt.
Approach the upside-down charger for a controlled regrasp. It must be laid flat in clear space to establish a reliable pins-down grasp.
Continue the side-grasp approach to the inverted charger, with open jaws and a continuous elbow-up wrist path.
Move around the exposed side of the inverted charger, continuing toward a shallow side grasp without touching the strip.
Bring the right gripper toward a horizontal side grasp of the inverted charger; keep the jaws open and the wrist clear of the tabletop.
Continue flattening the wrist for a side grasp of the clearly pins-up charger, keeping the fingers open during positioning.
Lower toward the charger’s sidewalls while leveling the open right gripper, avoiding the exposed upward pins.
Replan after the continuity guard: hold the wrist angle and use smaller downward steps with a slight inward reach to approach the charger sidewalls without extending the elbow further.
Pitch the open right fingers slightly down to reach the charger sidewalls while keeping the wrist height and elbow branch, with a small lateral centering correction.
Close around the inverted charger’s upper sidewalls and let the grasp settle before a small vertical retention test.
Lift the inverted charger gently to verify retention before moving it to clear table space for a flat placement and a better end grasp.
The inverted charger follows the lift. Move it away from the strip and begin tipping it for a flat placement on clear table space, keeping the grip closed.
The prior chunk was rejected without motion. Retry the lift-and-tip at half scale to maintain joint continuity.
Continue tipping the inverted charger toward horizontal while lifting it over clear table space, keeping a secure closed grasp.
